title: Spiral galaxy NGC 4911 in the Coma cluster
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 4911 in the Coma Cluster, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA). Acknowledgment: K. Cook (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, USA)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: Rich lanes of dust and gas near the center of this face-on spiral galaxy stand out against glowing clusters of newborn stars and pink clouds of hydrogen that signal ongoing star formation. This is NGC 4911, deep in the Coma Cluster, which the caption places 320 million light-years away, in the northern sky in Coma Berenices. Thousands of other galaxies fill the background.

Spirals near the cluster's center are being reshaped by their neighbors. Wispy arcs in the outer arms of NGC 4911 are being pulled and distorted by a companion, NGC 4911A, at upper right. The stripped material will eventually spread through the cluster core, feeding its stars and star clusters that drift between galaxies.

The Coma Cluster holds almost 1,000 galaxies, so interactions and collisions are frequent. When galaxies of similar mass merge, they form ellipticals, which is why ellipticals are more common near the crowded center.

understand.summary: This natural-color image combines Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 and Advanced Camera for Surveys, with blue, visible, H-alpha and near-infrared filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The colors aim to be natural, but 28 hours of exposure reveal faint detail far beyond anything the eye could see.

explore: This natural-color image needed 28 hours of exposure, combining data from Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 and Advanced Camera for Surveys. Hubble's sharp cameras and long exposures made the faint outer details visible.
alt: A face-on spiral galaxy with dark dust lanes near its center, pink hydrogen clouds, a companion galaxy at upper right, and many galaxies in the background.
